text: Room migration 5->6 has never been executed by any test

Covered, with one finding worth keeping.

Added:
- android AppDbMigrationTest — 1->6 and 5->6 against a database built at the old
  version, compared column-by-column against Room's own exported schema, plus
  row-survival and default checks. Mutation-checked: dropping a column, dropping
  a NOT NULL, and changing a DEFAULT are each caught.
- exportSchema = true, room.schemaLocation, and app/schemas/.../6.json committed.
- server test_closing.py — migration 7 executed, and its close_votes table
  compared structurally against the one schema.sql builds. Mutation-checked:
  removing closed_at and weakening the primary key are each caught.

FINDING — Room 2.8 cannot run migrations on the driver path. Migration
.migrate(SQLiteConnection) is TODO("Migration functionality with a SQLiteDriver
is not yet available") for anything but a support-backed connection, so all five
migrations would throw NotImplementedError at once if DatabaseModule ever adopted
setDriver(). Production is fine today: it uses the framework path. But every test
in the module uses BundledSQLiteDriver, because Robolectric has no working SQLite
on Linux/aarch64 (robolectric.properties pins LEGACY for the same reason), so the
obvious "make tests and production match" change is the dangerous one. Noted in
the test's header comment. Revisit when Room implements it.

Consequence for the test: it drives the migration objects directly through a
SupportSQLiteDatabase facade rather than opening a Room database, and checks the
result against the exported schema — the same comparison Room makes at runtime.
Room's own open-and-validate machinery stays uncovered, which is not our code.

Done in edc5b43. Android tests 4/4, and the full verify-all run is green:
server lint, server pytest, web vitest+tsc+lint, android test+lint.
